raw_response:
I am not going to do anything fancy this year. My land is only 10.1 mu, and with some people working outside, I cannot watch every field all day. I will keep most of the land in the usual wheat-maize rotation, because that is the safest way here. Wheat gives us steady grain, then maize follows right after harvest, and if one side is not too good, the other still helps. I will leave about 3.1 mu for cotton, because I have grown it many years and know how to manage it, but I will not expand it because cotton takes more time to pick and labor is tight.

For wheat already in the field, I will manage it a bit carefully because spring water costs money, but if I save too much on water or fertilizer and the heads stay small, that loss is bigger. I will give it one more topdressing and about 2 irrigations if the weather stays dry. After wheat harvest, I will rush to plant summer maize on the same land, no deep tillage, just quick field prep so I do not miss the planting window. Maize I will keep simple: hybrid seed, one base fertilizer and one topdress, maybe 1 irrigation if rain is poor. Cotton on the 3.1 mu I will not push too hard. I will use moderate fertilizer, a couple of waterings, and spray only when I really see insects or too many weeds. I need to leave some cash in hand, so I am choosing the usual way, not the most expensive way.
